*Spl-uh!* This code is a security DISASTER wrapped in a UX nightmare! The developer may have followed the mockups, but they clearly skipped security class. Let me break down this train wreck:

## Critical Issues 🚨

**Line 20-22 - Storing tokens in localStorage (CRITICAL)**
Using localStorage for auth tokens = sitting duck for XSS attacks! Any injected script can steal these tokens. Use httpOnly cookies instead so JavaScript can't access them. This is Authentication 101!

**Line 38-39, 64 - XSS Vulnerabilities (CRITICAL)**
`dangerouslySetInnerHTML` with user-controlled error messages and bio fields? Guh! An attacker can inject `<script>alert(document.cookie)</script>` and pwn every user who views it. Use plain text rendering or properly sanitize with DOMPurify.

**Line 58-60 - Storing passwords in localStorage (CRITICAL)**
ARE YOU KIDDING ME?! Never, EVER store passwords client-side! This "remember me" feature just hands credentials to attackers on a silver platter. Just save the email if anything.

**Line 123 - eval() with user input (CRITICAL)**
`eval('window.trackSignup("' + formData.email + '")')` - This is a code injection vulnerability! An attacker enters email: `"); malicious_code(); ("` and boom, arbitrary code execution. Use proper function calls, not string concatenation in eval!

## High Severity Issues

**Line 46-49, 111-114 - No error handling (HIGH)**
Signup and password reset make API calls with zero try-catch blocks. Users see white screens when networks fail. The UX should be fashionable AND functional!

**Line 154 - Email in URL parameters (HIGH)**
`?email=${email}` exposes email addresses in server logs, browser history, and referrer headers. Use POST requests for sensitive data!

**Line 167 - Sensitive data in URL query (HIGH)**
`?message=Password reset successful` leaks password reset status. Use session-based messages instead.

**Line 184 - Missing Bearer prefix (HIGH)**
Authorization header should be `Bearer ${token}`, not just the raw token. Many APIs reject improperly formatted headers.

**Line 196-200 - Client-side admin check (HIGH)**
Checking admin status from localStorage?! An attacker just opens DevTools and types `localStorage.setItem('user_data', '{"role":"admin"}')`. Admin checks MUST happen server-side!

## Medium Issues

**Lines 96-100 - Weak client-side validation (MEDIUM)**
Password requirements only checked client-side. Attackers bypass this by calling the API directly. Server must validate too!

**Line 242 - Token in URL (MEDIUM)**
`?token=${getAuthToken()}` in beacon request exposes tokens in logs. Use POST body or headers.

**Missing CSRF protection (MEDIUM)**
No CSRF tokens anywhere! State-changing operations need anti-CSRF measures.

**No input sanitization (MEDIUM)**
Email/password fields accept any characters. Validate format and length server-side.

**No loading states (LOW)**
Buttons should disable during async operations to prevent double-submissions.

**No accessibility attributes (LOW)**
Missing aria-labels, error announcements, and proper form associations.

## Verdict: **REJECT** ❌

This needs a complete security overhaul before it's safe to ship. The users will NOT love data breaches!
